gloss: hair at the back of the head; lingering attachment

definitions.gloss: hair at the back of the head
definitions.explanation: The hair growing at the back of one's head.
A feeling of being unable to leave something behind, as if someone were pulling you back by the hair. Used primarily in the idiom 後ろ髪を引かれる.

examples.japanese: {後|うし}ろ{髪|がみ}をまとめる。
examples.english: To tie up the hair at the back of one's head.

examples.japanese: {後|うし}ろ{髪|がみ}が{首|くび}にかかる。
examples.english: The hair at the back touches the neck.

examples.japanese: {後|うし}ろ{髪|がみ}が{伸|の}びてきたので、{美容院|びよういん}に{行|い}かなければ。
examples.english: The hair at the back of my head has gotten long, so I need to go to the salon.

examples.japanese: {後|うし}ろ{髪|がみ}を{引|ひ}かれる{思|おも}い。
{故郷|ふるさと}を{離|はな}れるのは{後|うし}ろ{髪|がみ}を{引|ひ}かれた。
examples.english: Leaving my hometown was hard to do — I felt pulled back.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}を{預|あず}けて{出勤|しゅっきん}するのは、{毎朝|まいあさ}{後|うし}ろ{髪|がみ}を{引|ひ}かれる{思|おも}いだ。
examples.english: Leaving my child behind and going to work feels like a reluctant parting every morning.

notes:
The literal meaning (sense 1) refers to the hair at the back of the head, but the word is far more commonly encountered in the idiomatic expression {後|うし}ろ{髪|がみ}を{引|ひ}かれる (sense 2).

IDIOM:
The expression {後|うし}ろ{髪|がみ}を{引|ひ}かれる literally means "to have one's hair pulled from behind" — evoking the image of being physically held back as you try to leave. It expresses deep reluctance to part with someone or something, a strong emotional pull to stay.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {後|うし}ろ{髪|がみ}を{引|ひ}かれる — to feel reluctant to leave; to feel a lingering attachment
- {後|うし}ろ{髪|がみ}を{引|ひ}かれる{思|おも}い — a feeling of lingering reluctance
- {後|うし}ろ{髪|がみ}を{引|ひ}かれながら — while reluctantly leaving

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {未練|みれん} — lingering attachment, regret; a broader term for reluctance to let go
- {名残惜|なごりお}しい — sad to part; a direct expression of reluctance at parting
